title: The God Who Sees It All

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth. - Gen 6:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
At first glance this looks like a simple line of record-keeping - just the names of Noah's three sons. It would be easy to pass over. But this quiet verse is doing important work. In the middle of a dark account of a corrupt world facing judgement, God pauses to name the family He is about to save. These three names - Shem, Ham, and Japheth - are the thread of hope running through the darkness.

God knows His people by name. Even as He surveys a world gone wrong, He has His eye on the household He will preserve. The vast story of judgement does not swallow up the individuals God intends to rescue. He notices them, names them, and carries them safely through.

This is a great comfort. In a world of billions, God has not lost sight of you. He is not a distant deity managing masses; He knows His own by name. Jesus said the Good Shepherd "calls his own sheep by name" (John 10:3). You are not a number to God.

And through these three sons, God would repopulate the earth and, in time, bring forth the Saviour through Shem's line. What looks like a simple list is really the preserving of God's redemptive plan. The God who named Noah's sons knows your name too, and He is weaving your life into His good purposes.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God knows you personally, by name?
- How does it comfort you that God does not lose sight of individuals?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that in a world of billions, You know me by name. Thank You that I am not lost in the crowd to You. Weave my life into Your good purposes, as You did Noah's family.
